chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Sa'd ibn Abd Allah both said: Ayyub ibn Nuh narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Exalted: 'And know that Allah intervenes between man and his heart.' He (AS) said: 'He intervenes between him and the belief that falsehood is truth.' And it has been said: 'Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, intervenes between man and his heart through death.' And Abu Abdillah (AS) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, transfers the servant from misery to happiness, but does not transfer him from happiness to misery.'
Chapter: The Negation of Predestination (Al-Jabr) and Delegation (Al-Tafwid)
ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq interpret Allah's intervention between man and his heart in Surah Al-Imran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that divine intervention in the heart primarily manifests as the capacity to distinguish truth from falsehood, a key mechanism in the Shia doctrine of divine justice (Adl). This narration supports the middle path between absolute predestination (Jabr) and total delegation (Tafwid), affirming that while God facilitates the transition from misery to happiness, He does not arbitrarily cast a righteous servant back into error, thereby preserving human agency within divine decree.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 6. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alSaffar and Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah both said: Ayyub ibn Nuh said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim that

Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) was asked to interpret the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: And know that Allah intervenes between man and his heart. He (AS) said: “He intervenes between man and the belief that falsehood is the righteous.” It is also said: “Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, intervenes between man and his heart through death.” Abu `Abd Allah (AS) said: “Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, brings people from adversity to privilege, but does not bring people for privilege to adversity.”
